summary: Resume-event header misalignment after long-lived proxy buffering causes out-of-order chunks and missing finish marker
description: Customers report that after a transient network interruption through their corporate proxy, resumed SSE connections receive a burst of tokens delivered out-of-order, and the stream never emits the terminal 'done' event. The model continues producing tokens server-side but client-side assembly is missing the finalizer metadata. This appears only when connections pass through the customer's HTTP proxy that buffers/chunks responses for long-lived requests.
impact: Multiple BrightRetail users experience corrupted generated text (duplicate fragments, ordering issues) and finalization isn't observed, causing the product to hang on 'waiting for end' and retry logic to double-submit prompts. Affects ~10% of streaming sessions for this customer since 2026-03-10 after they updated proxy firmware.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use BrightRetail's corporate proxy (they provided a repro VM config). 2) Start an SSE streaming generation with a 2k token output. 3) Interrupt TCP (simulated 15s pause) between SSE chunks. 4) Allow client to reconnect using resume token flow. 5) Observe assembled output on client side and protocol events. Note: reproducible only when proxy applies response chunk coalescing / gzip buffering.
observed_behavior: After reconnect, client receives a flurry of small SSE 'data:' events where order of fragments does not match server offsets. The 'meta: finish' event that indicates stream completion is not received by the client; server-side logs still show model completion and final 'emit_finish' in runtime. Client retries lead to duplicated partial tokens in downstream UI.
expected_behavior: Resume should continue the stream from the last acknowledged token in-order and deliver the finalization metadata exactly once (or perform an explicit 'end' event). No duplication or reordering should occur.

initial_triage: Suspect interaction between our SSE resume semantics (per-chunk metadata headers including offset and finalizer) and third-party proxy buffering. Proxy appears to coalesce/fling buffered segments at reconnect time which breaks ordering of logical chunk boundaries and hides the final 'done' marker in a separate TCP flush.
investigation_notes:
- Confirmed server emitted ordered chunks and 'emit_finish' in logs.
- Packet capture from customer's edge shows proxy buffering multiple SSE events and then writing them in a different order when reconnect resumed.
- Repro in internal environment only when we enable a synthetic buffering proxy that reorders flushes.
- Hypothesis: our resume logic relies on per-event framing plus immediate flush for 'meta: finish'. If proxy delays flushes and merges chunks, client may parse events in the wrong logical order or drop the finalizer due to intermediate split boundaries.
- Possible contributing factor: gzip compression at proxy layer can change chunk boundaries and our client-side parser assumes chunk alignments for resume offsets.
mitigation_attempts:
- Asked BrightRetail to temporarily disable response buffering/compression on proxy for streaming endpoints — reduces occurrences to near zero.
- Implemented client-side defensive parsing to accept out-of-order offsets and buffer until finalizer observed (customer-side patch).
- Applied a gateway-side workaround to add explicit heartbeat 'keepalive' SSE events and force SSE flush after critical metadata events in a canary for us-east dedicated nodes.
current_status: Canary with explicit flush enabled on a subset of us-east serving nodes. Customer-side mitigation validated. Working with infra team to propose permanent server-side change and recommend proxy config to customers.
next_steps: 1) Engineering: design server-side resume protocol change to make finalizer idempotent and independent of chunk flush timing (ticket assigned to runtime team). 2) Docs: add proxy configuration guidance to 'streaming runbook'. 3) Customer Success: assist BrightRetail to patch proxy or apply config to disable chunk coalescing for Redwood endpoints. 4) Monitor canary for 48 hours and collect metrics on resume success rate.
resolution: (open) No final resolution yet — customer temporary workaround in place; server-side fix in design. Will update when runtime change is merged and rolled out.
estimated_impact_reduction: Temporary workaround reduces affected sessions from ~10% to <1% for BrightRetail. Canary for explicit flush reduced reorders observed in telemetry by ~92% in the test cohort.
